proposals: The Department of Food and Public Distribution should publish storage capacity every quarter on one fixed basis, split into FCI and state agencies, owned and hired, covered and CAP, so figures such as 371.93, about 482 and 917.83 LMT can be reconciled rather than read as one series.

The Food Corporation of India should publish the rent it pays each year for hired storage, by state and by lessor type, so the cost of renting about 70 per cent of its capacity can be compared with the cost of owning it.

The Ministry of Cooperation should publish a godown-level tracker for the PACS storage plan, listing units sanctioned, completed and in use with capacity and location, so progress toward the additional 700 LMT and the 2,150 LMT total can be checked year by year.

The Department of Food and Public Distribution should report in its monthly Foodgrain Bulletin how much central-pool stock sits in open CAP storage, so a squeeze like the roughly 907 LMT peak of 2021 is visible as it builds rather than afterwards.
